correctness.rationale: The exact pair equations give x=h/(h+2theta(2+theta)), z=(1+theta)x and EV²=theta z/2; both finite moment formulas match 409 exact-rational assertions across 49 independently solved finite stationary systems. The infinite proof uses the exact count generator, a uniform stationary O(h) imbalance bound, Jacobi/Beta stationary moments and a fast-scale characteristic-function ODE with explicit O(sqrt(h)) jump remainder and O(sqrt(h)) mixed correction, valid for any two diverging class sizes. Gaussian mixture and kurtosis follow from beta integrals. Finite checks are auxiliary; no computational finite cutoff is claimed to prove an infinite limit.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Generic network theories are examined as potential subsumption. Pair approximation is not an exact biclique theorem; general duality can derive finite correlations but not by itself specify the conditional fast limiting law; complete-graph single-density Beta behavior has no separate class-disagreement coordinate. A possible uninspected broad multiscale theorem remains an explicit residual risk.

value.rationale: The two-part discrepancy is a canonical local heterogeneity observable hidden by the aggregate opinion density. The finding proves its critical-order fluctuations form a beta-mixed normal, not a simple Gaussian, computes a nonzero exact asymptotic excess kurtosis for every lambda, and stays valid with no ratio restriction. This is structural second-order information about a standard class of network Markov chains, not arbitrary parametrization or a known table recomputation.
